TargetProcessId
The unique ID of a target process (in decimal, non-hex format). This field exists in almost all events, and it represents the ID of the
process that is responsible for the activity of the event in focus. For example, the TargetProcessId of a process that performed
thread injection in an InjectedThread event
SHA256HashData
The SHA256 hash of a file. In most cases, the hash of the file referred to by the ImageFileName field.

PatternDisposition
PatternDisposition is a bitfield value that represents actions taken by the Falcon sensor in response to malicious activity. Bit values
come from response bits and modifier bits, where response bits are actions taken or attempted, and modifier bits are reasons the
attempt was unsuccessful. If PatternDisposition’s value is 0, no response was attempted. For example:
If PatternDisposition’s value is 1040, it will be made up of 2 bits, KILL_PROCESS(16) and OPERATION_BLOCKED(1024).
Look up your value in the Most Common Bitfield for PatternDisposition table. Once you have its response and modifier bit names,
you can find their descriptions in the PatternDisposition Bit table below. Please note, your response may contain one or more
response bits.
